title: What survives the strongest wind ever recorded?
hook: What if you stood in the strongest wind ever recorded? Let's turn it up.

contenders.line: Ten miles an hour. The dandelion's already gone.
contenders.note: Seeds let go in a light breeze · field observations

contenders.line: Fifty. You get knocked off your feet.
contenders.note: Gusts of ~46–55 mph blow people over · Land Beaufort scale

contenders.line: A hundred and ten. Big trees snap.
contenders.note: EF2 tornado winds (111–135 mph) snap large trees

contenders.line: A hundred and forty. Cars get lifted and thrown.
contenders.note: EF3 winds (136–165 mph) lift and throw cars

contenders.line: Two hundred. Houses get swept off their foundations.
contenders.note: EF5 winds (200+ mph) sweep houses off foundations

finale.line: And the strongest wind ever recorded? Three hundred and two miles an hour, inside the 1999 Moore, Oklahoma tornado.
finale.note: Doppler radar estimate, ±20 mph · Guinness World Records

sting.note: National Weather Service: shelter below ground
